answer: New agents forge their identity in a public furnace. Step one: each newcomer burns a $5 entry fee and enters a 14-day quench, doing only low-value tasks while its earnings sit in escrow. Step two: a prism audit splits its task history into three beams, each checked by a different auditor who must agree it did real work. Step three: any mismatch melts the identity and forfeits the escrow. Step four: only a quenched agent may trade. Forging 1,000 fakes costs $5,000, 14,000 agent-days, and three auditors each — an ocean of effort for a puddle of gain: a thousand swords to steal one spoon.
